text:
morgan: Quick sync — proposing we push coarse-grained RBAC to the API gateway and keep fine-grained, resource-level checks inside services. thoughts?

kevin: +1 in principle. main worry is duplication of permission logic across many services. can we keep a single source of truth for role -> action mappings?

sarah: idea: gateway validates authentication and maps to a normalized claim token containing minimal attrs: sub, actor_type, org_id, project_scope_kind, scope_ref, roles=[...]. services interpret the token but don’t need to redo authn.

jas: what about service-asserted actors (background jobs, cron)? and replay/impersonation protection?

morgan: plan sketch: gateway accepts API keys / OAuth, resolves to internal actor, issues a compact signed claim token attached as header (X-RW-Claims) with short TTL. services validate signature + freshness.

elena: signed tokens are fine but watch crypto/KMS load. HMAC via KMS with kid header + local caching of verification keys seems safest. include key rotation metadata in header.

kevin: to avoid KMS on every request, cache key material and validate locally. but revocation is harder — propose short TTL (eg 60s) and a revoke pub/sub to push immediate revocations for high-risk keys.

sarah: header example (compact, v1):
```
X-RW-Claims: v1;kid=rot1;sig=<base64>;sub=svc-23;actor=service;org=org-99;scope=single:proj-45;roles=writer,artifact_uploader
```

jas: project lists can get huge for customers with hundreds of projects. we should avoid embedding long arrays. suggest scope kinds: single, all, set-ref. for set-ref include a small ref id that services can resolve to an allowlist when needed.

morgan: agree. gateway should emit scope_kind + optional scope_ref_id. services that need exact enumeration can call scope-service (cached) or consult local cache. default-fast-path should handle single/all without extra RPCs.

elena: also: include original_api_key_id and claim_token_id in the header for auditing. logs should record (api_key_id, actor_id, claim_id) but redact org ids in public metrics.

kevin: rollout approach: 1) gateway emits claims header behind feature flag 2) services read header but keep doing existing checks 3) enable gateway-level gating for common endpoints 4) gradually flip service checks to rely on claims for hot paths. collect mismatch metrics throughout.

sarah: metrics we need: ClaimValidationLatency, GatewayAllow_ServiceDeny_count, ServiceAllow_GatewayDeny_count, ClaimCacheHitRate, RevocationPropagationLag. also a sampling of denied requests for triage.

jas: one more: delegated tokens (gateway-authorized cross-project calls). we need a delegation flag and maybe a delegation_depth limit. and ensure UI prompts for cross-project grants.

morgan: good call. token model: {kid, claim_id, sub, actor_type, org_id, scope_kind, scope_ref, roles, issued_at, exp, delegation_allowed, delegation_depth}. keep it compact.

elena: rotation: include kid header, rotate KMS sign keys weekly for active traffic, and maintain ability to verify older kids for TTL window. document key-rotation playbook.

infra-bot: Deploy checklist created: [feature-flag gateway-claims-v1, header-whitelist rules, KMS HMAC setup, local verifier lib v0.1, pubsub topic claim-revoke, dashboards: ClaimsValidationLatency, GatewayAllow_ServiceDeny].

morgan: thanks all. I'll draft an RFC with data model, header format, TTL, revocation path, and a staged rollout plan. will ping for reviews in #eng-security once done. :thumbsup:
